notes: Base: base_commit is the worktree HEAD before the first commit. The pin is 49467335d288 (a git worktree outside the repository, removed at the end). The three live bundles were fetched by get-object with the version ids the signed packet names, untarred to scratch, and used as the build input; each bundle holds 45 entries.

Bytes: for 49financial the folded sha256 of the live and of the pin holdings_snapshot.py equal the values in the v2 record. The other two bundles were not re-hashed; their producer bytes are the ones the builds imported.

Builds: one subprocess per tree per firm (python -I; the producer and lib are put first on sys.path and the imported module is asserted to lie under its tree). Source objects are read through the producer's own VersionedInputs. Run 1 pin builds had no receipts seed (they define the receipts); every other build read only the pinned receipts (meta.source_reads_outside_seed 0). The run-1 identity build re-read the same run-1 objects (identity_reads_outside_seed equal to the run-1 count), and the run-2 identity build read none outside the seed.
Refusals: the S3 client wrapper refuses every operation whose name does not begin with get_, list_ or head_; refused_calls is 0 in every build of every firm.

Gate: each code's own candidate, after the producer's recompute of weights, is evaluated with the tree's own evaluate_publish_gate, directory_marks_no_closures and closed_account_ids bound to the firm's bucket, against the served publication read by begin() and served_publication() (read calls only). Outcomes: 49financial PUBLISHED on both codes; cottonwood REFUSED on account_lost for the live code and PUBLISHED for the pin; inflection REFUSED on source_frontier_older on both codes at pin 2026-10-13.

Business date: the candidate's clocks business_date read 2026-10-12 on both codes for all three firms (inflection's pin is 2026-10-13, so its candidate is dated one trading day earlier). The snapshot-level clocks were not compared node by node; this business date is the only clocks value reported.

Comparison: rows by node_kind; ACCOUNT node ids on each side; every numeric leaf of every node on both codes with an absolute tolerance of 0.01; the four classification fields raw; and a short hash of the non-numeric residue of every top-level field. Nodes present on one side only: 0 on every firm. Numeric changes beyond tolerance: 0 on every firm (largest_abs_delta 0.0). Every changed node is therefore a classification change.

Signed cash rule (identity-patch): the pin is rebuilt in this process with apply_cash_rule replaced by the identity function. A node is signed when the pin's asset_class differs from the identity value and the live asset_class equals the identity value. The counts are 32, 249 and 841, equal to the signed counts.

Cottonwood: 236 changed nodes beyond the signed rule (asset_class 4 fixed_income to cash, asset_class_basis 236 (NAME_ALIAS or NAME_PATTERN to TABLE), sub_asset_class 51) are each reproduced by the holdings_snapshot.py member swap alone; no other member reproduces any of them. For the 4 asset_class nodes the identity build also yields cash, so their move is not the rule's effect. The sub-cause inside holdings_snapshot.py (keyed gate, CUSIP fallback, multi_asset line, account_id, exemption repair) is not separated by this measurement; the member is the unit of attribution.

Commits: the commits attributed to the holdings_snapshot.py member swap are its history commits at the pin whose subjects name account_id, keyed, CUSIP, SC-e-56 or multi_asset (case-insensitive). Five match (f3a42b2ab8, 7ace854890, 3f2bdda578, 9efbec3c2f, 4cc72587d6). A case-insensitive subject search of the same history for CUSIP found none. The signed cash rule is attributed by identity-patch, not by commit.

Hybrids: one hybrid per behaviour or data member of the firm's packet v2 table (49financial 19, cottonwood 21, inflection 20). Two cottonwood hybrids needed one pin-only module each and were given it alone, recorded in hybrid_extra_pin_files: the build_cottonwood_mdpf_slice.py hybrid needs silver/opal_unidentified.py, which the v2 table does not list and no live bundle holds (the pin's own cottonwood build imports it); the rebalancer_schemas.py hybrid needs silver/opal_strategy_matcher.py, which the table lists as added. No hybrid of 49financial or inflection needed a module copy. The 49financial and inflection processes started before the module-copy retry was added to the harness; the retry path is the only difference, and no hybrid of those firms reached it.

Determinism: run 2 rebuilt the pin candidate, the pin identity candidate and the live candidate on the run-1 receipts. The receipts, the gate results and the comparison result were equal to run 1 on every firm. The hybrid signatures were built once and reused by both comparisons. The digests are sha256 over the canonical JSON of each comparison result.
Mutant: one SECURITY node's pin asset_class was replaced in memory (run 1 signatures). The changed-node count rose by exactly one on every firm.

Not read or written: no write, upload, invoke, send or sign call was made (refused_calls 0). The served publication was read only through the gate's summary. The directory entries and the account identifiers were used in memory and are not recorded here. No node id, account id or holding name is in this record; the per-node signatures, receipts, gate summaries and logs are outside the repository and were removed at the end.
Runtime: 6390 s for 49financial, 4647 s for cottonwood and 3729 s for inflection, the three processes running concurrently.

Premise: packet v2 section 6 reads inflection PUBLISHED before and after the release; this measurement reads REFUSED on both codes (surprise row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W384-S2). The packet's own sha256 is not computed; both halves are UNSIGNED.
